title: Washington cleared Nvidia chip buyers whose offices were empty, report finds
summary: The Commerce Department has approved Chinese firms to handle Nvidia's H200 accelerators even where the companies have little visible presence, according to a New York Times investigation summarised by The Verge. Reporters found New Matrix's listed office empty, with no directory entry for the 17-month-old company at its address or at the industrial park's property manager. Its owners are tied to a private equity firm blacklisted by Washington since 2024. The report describes the case as part of a pattern rather than a single lapse.
